title: Annotatio III §.X (6): Ratio / Philosophy theoretical — overturns substance, accident, spirit, body, place, penetration
pass_a_gloss: (6.) To cleaner Reason, i.e. to Philosophy, both Theoretical and Practical. To the former indeed, while it inverts and shakes the essential Ideas and Definitions of the first and chief things — Substance and Accident, Spirit and Body, Penetrability and Impenetrability, Extension and Locality — by stripping a Finite and defined Substance of its essential accidents, absolving Accidents from actual Inherence in a substance, changing Christ’s body and blood into spirit by denying them extension, impenetration and locality essentially owed to human bodies, and so to be destituted not even by miracles by the Author of all finite essences unto one, although as most powerful Annihilator also at His pleasure, yet admitting no contradictories meanwhile, and that through and because of His omnipotence.
pass_b_english: It overturns essential ideas of substance and accident, spirit and body, penetrability, extension, locality: strips finite substance of essential accidents, frees accidents from inherence, spirits Christ’s body by denying extension, impenetrability, and place — which even omnipotence will not admit as contradictories via miracle.
source_text: (6.) Rationi Emaculatiori, i. e. Philosophiæ, tùm Theoreticæ, tum Practicæ. Priori quidem, dum primarum ac præcipuarum rerum, Substantiæ puta & Accidentis, Spiritus & Corporis, Penetrabilitatis & Impenetrabilitatis, Extensionis & Localitatis essentiales Ideas ac Definitiones invertit ac concutit, Substantiam Finitam definitamque accidentibus suis essentialibus exuendo, Accidentia ab Inhæsione, in substantia, actuali absolvendo, corpus & sanguinem Christi in spiritum commutando, per negatam iisdem tum extensionem, tùm impenetrationem tùm localitatem, humanis corporibus essentialiter debitas, indeque nec per miracula, ab essentiarum ad unum omnium finitarum Autore, etsi pro Lubitu suô Annihilatore quoque potentissimo, contradictoria interim nulla, idque per & propter omnipotentiam suam, admissuro, destituendas.
